device.description: 12-bit dual-channel ultralow-glitch voltage-output DAC, two's complement input (power-on mid scale), 50 MHz SPI interface, IOVDD level shifters, daisy-chain SDO and asynchronous clear
device.note: dac7553.pdf (SLAS477) p.4 power requirements (VDD, IOVDD 2.7-5.5 V; IOVDD down to 1.8 V, note 3), p.5 timing characteristics and serial write operation, p.6 pin description (RGT) and terminal functions (CLR sets 000H = mid scale), p.14 serial interface programming (Table 1) and power-down mode control (Table 2), p.15 power-on reset (mid scale), p.16 asynchronous clear, serial interface (DCEN low: the SYNC rising edge after the 16th bit updates the DACs), 2s-complement data format

pages: p.4 (supplies), p.5 (timing), p.6 (pins), p.14 (Tables 1-2), p.15 (power-on reset), p.16 (clear, serial interface, data format)
notModeled: analog outputs, references and VFB sense inputs (never driven)
power-down output loads: stored per channel in PWR only; how a powered-down channel returns to normal operation is not described
PD pin (pin 7, 'power-down'): function and polarity not described in the datasheet; a plain input
daisy-chain mode (DCEN high): SDO repeating SDIN with a 16-clock delay and latching the last 16 bits at SYNC rising are not modeled; SDO stays Hi-Z (the DCEN-low behavior)
input data are two's complement (800H = 0 V, 000H = mid scale); registers store the code as written
CLR resets all registers and the DAC updates at the first SYNC rising edge after CLR returns high: modeled as an immediate clear to code 0
SCLK limits (50 MHz, 10 MHz with SDO) and setup/hold times
variants: DAC7552 (dac7552.pdf) is the same chip with straight-binary coding and zero-scale power-on; own spec file. Table 1 on p.14 lists DAC(s) B for the 0110 and A for the 1000 rows; the function text (same as DAC7552) is followed.
